Apple 希望在美国对 App Store 外部的购买收取最高 15% 的佣金
发布者
admin
标签：
Apple
、
Epic Games
Apple 与 Epic Games 之间的法律战又出现了新的转折。近日，Apple 向法院提交了一份声明，请求撤销一项对其施加的禁令。这涉及美国 iOS 应用内购买的佣金问题。

在这份文件中，Apple 提醒法院，2024 年因一项法院裁决，它被要求允许开发者将美国用户引导至 App Store 之外进行支付。为了弥补自身支出，Apple 对此类支付引入了 27% 的专项费用。然而，负责该案的法官 Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers 对此并不满意，并于 2025 年春季禁止 Apple 从 App Store 外部的购买中收取任何费用。

如今，Apple 正试图恢复佣金制度，尽管有所调整。它向法院提交了一份新的费用结构，降低了百分比。修订后的结构如下：

- “标准应用”中的购买收取 15% 的佣金；
- 来自特定联盟计划的应用内购买以及订阅续费收取 10% 的佣金；
- 年收入低于 100 万美元的开发者所开发应用中的购买收取 5% 的佣金。

Apple 解释称，这些费率使其能够收回“至少部分补偿”，以覆盖其向开发者提供的工具、技术和服务的成本。

值得注意的是，App Store 的标准佣金为 30%，Apple 无意更改这一比例。

Epic Games 已经对 Apple 的行为提出批评，称该提议结构“远远超出了第九巡回法院关于允许费用的指导意见的范围”。Epic Games 计划在 60 天内提交一份附有专家意见的正式反对书。

Apple wants to charge up to a 15% commission on purchases outside the App Store in the U.S.
Published by
admin
Tags:
Apple
,
Epic Games
Another twist in the legal battle between Apple and Epic Games. Recently, Apple
filed
a statement in court, requesting to overturn one of the prohibitions imposed on it. This pertains to the commission for in-app purchases on iOS in the United States.
In the document, the corporation reminded the court that in 2024, due to a court ruling, it was required to allow developers to redirect American users for payments outside the App Store. To compensate for its expenses, Apple introduced a special fee of 27% for such payments. However, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers, who is overseeing the case, was not satisfied with this, and in the spring of 2025, she prohibited Apple from taking any money from purchases made outside the App Store.
Now Apple is attempting to reinstate the commission, albeit with changes. It has presented a new fee structure with lower percentages to the court. The revised structure is as follows:
a 15% commission for purchases in “standard apps”;
a 10% commission for purchases in apps from certain affiliate programs and for subscription renewals;
a 5% commission for purchases in apps from developers with annual revenue of less than $1 million.
Apple explained that the rates would let it recoup “at least some compensation” for its tools, technologies, and services it provides to developers.
It should be noted that the standard commission in the App Store is 30%, which Apple does not intend to change.
Epic Games has already criticized Apple’s actions, stating that the proposed structure “far outside of the bounds of the Ninth Circuit’s guidance on permissible fees”. Within 60 days, Epic Games plans to file an official objection with expert comments.

Project Rise (Supercell)
Supercell’s long-in-gestation action RPG spin-off of Clash of Clans seems to be edging closer to launch: the Finnish firm is opening a
beta test for Project Rise beginning August 19,
which runs until September 2.
The project was first revealed as Clash Heroes way back in 2021, but it was
rebooted and renamed in 2024 as Project Rise
. There’s been very little news on the title since.
Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed (THQ Nordic Mobile)
Snapshot Games’ mobile port of Purple Lamp’s 3D platformer remake launches on iOS and Android on September 16, priced at $15.99. It’s now open for pre-orders.
Dave the Diver (Mintrocket)
Mintrocket’s hit RPG-management sim launches on iOS and Android on September 17, complete with the Dredge and In the Jungle DLC packs included at launch.
Goat Simulator 3 (Coffee Stain North)
Coffee Stain North’s open-world sandbox sequel is now available on Android through Google Play Pass, bundling the base game with all its free seasonal content updates.
Little Kitty, Big City (Double Dagger Studio)
Double Dagger Studio’s cat-adventure hit, which has sold over 10m copies on PC and console, is coming to mobile later this year. There’s no firm release date yet, but a first trailer is out now.
SoulTerra Odyssey (Bandai Namco Entertainment)
This new soft lainch from Bandai Namco appears to be a midcore match 3D roguelite RPG. It was soft-launched August 6 and is currently live only in the Philippines.
Slots & Daggers (Future Friends Games)
Indie developer Friedemann’s slot machine roguelike, published by Future Friends Games, is already a hit on Steam with 300,000 copies sold. It’s coming to iOS and Android on August 17.
Greedy Greedy Gnomes (Future Friends Games)
Indie dev Nautlander’s incremental pot-breaking RPG is out now on PC via Steam ($5.99/£5.29/€6.15) and Android via Google Play ($3.99/£3.59). There’s no news on an iOS version as yet.
Azur Promilia (Nexon)
아주르
This open-world anime RPG from Nexon is currently in pre-order and looks slated for a soft launch only in South Korea.
小冰冰斗蛐蛐 (Farlight)
This appears to be a midcore auto-battler from Shanghai Lilith’s Farlight label, spun off from the studio’s existing “Xiao Bingbing” IP.
The game is in pre-registration and it looks like it has soft launched in China only ahead of an wider October 31 release. No official English title has been announced yet.
Kaboomania (Fancy Factory)
Fancy Factory’s retro maze-bomber is out now on iOS, alongside PC, console and original Amiga hardware, with a soundtrack from Amiga composer Chris Huelsbeck.
Cueva de las Manos (Philipp Stollenmayer)
An Apple Vision Pro puzzle game that 3D scans your living room into a Stone Age cave, Cueva de las Manos lets you solve shadow-based physics puzzles with your own hands. It’s out now, only on Apple’s Vision Pro store.

articles.summary: 文章认为游戏行业传统的定期续作模式正在失效，消费者更渴望“事件”式的新鲜体验，行业需要从连续发行转向提供独特、可分享的事件内容。
articles.translated_content:
现代消费者渴望“事件”，游戏行业需要提供事件 | 观点

如果你点击链接并购买了商品，我们可能会获得少量佣金。
请阅读我们的编辑政策。
.
几乎自从游戏行业诞生以来，关于续作的传统智慧一直保持不变：趁热打铁。如果你有一款热门游戏，确保在公众失去兴趣之前推出续作。如果你连续拥有多款热门作品，那就形成了一个系列，而这些系列需要稳定的发布节奏，以确保品牌势头不会衰减。
无论人们对无休止的续作泛滥翻多少白眼，或者多么渴望更多原创游戏，都从未动摇过这一无情的逻辑。成功的游戏获得了快速续作；真正成功的游戏催生了系列，发行商会竭尽全力以尽可能规律的节奏推出这些系列。在一些最大的系列中，发行商甚至会在不同迭代之间轮换不同的开发工作室，以确保当一款新作发售时，下一款已经在深度开发中。
我在这里使用过去时是故意的，因为在过去十年左右的时间里，这种对待续作和系列的方式已经显著动摇。瞄准年度发布的系列已基本消失。除了少数坚持年度发布节奏的体育游戏之外，《使命召唤》基本上是最后一个仍在坚持年度化的系列。续作之间的间隔也大幅拉长。如今，一款成功游戏与其续作之间相隔五六年已是常态。而在不久之前，到那时市场上应该已经有三四款作品了（或者在很多情况下，该系列早已在收益递减的锋利刀刃上消亡）。
《使命召唤》是除体育游戏之外少数仍在坚持年度化的系列之一 | 图片来源：动视
这一变化的部分原因是现实层面的。游戏开发时间比以往更长，而发售后续内容（DLC）的能力意味着，全价续作需要证明自己的价值，而不仅仅是提供不显著改变核心游戏体验的新内容。你也可以合理地 argue 指出，有些游戏走向了相反的方向——它们没有放弃快速发布节奏，而是更加深入地拥抱了它，成为每年多次推出重大新内容的服务型游戏。
然而，即使不考虑这些因素，观众对续作和系列的偏好显然也发生了显著变化。这并不是说那些呼吁减少续作、增加原创内容的呼声“赢了”。如果说有什么变化，那反而是更加根深蒂固的——观众评估媒体内容并决定如何分配金钱和注意力的根本方式已经发生了转变，这种转变对规律性系列发布并不友好。
这种消费者行为的转变远远超出了游戏领域——事实上，在其他媒体中，主要是电影中，更容易看到它的直接影响。今年暑期档的主要大片就是一个很好的例子。观影本身显然仍能与观众产生共鸣；在过去几个月里，我们看到大型旗舰大片冲向十亿美元大关（《奥德赛》和《蜘蛛侠：崭新之日》），独立恐怖电影凭借惊人的口碑获得了超出预算数个数量级的票房（《痴迷》和《后室》），以及多年前电影的续作表现强劲（距离上一部《玩具总动员》已有七年，距离原版《穿普拉达的女王》已有二十年）。
另一方面，显然这里并没有一套精准的公式在起作用，因为今年夏天也有很多大片未能吸引观众走进多厅影院。有些在商业上还算可以——《小黄人与怪兽》只是相对于票房预期和该系列此前的作品令人失望——但其他一些，如《曼达洛人与古古》、《海洋奇缘》和《女超人》，几乎可以肯定亏了钱，并让整个系列和电影宇宙都受到了质疑。
你当然可以逐一分析这些电影，找出它们表现好或不好的原因，但我认为所有这些案例都有一条共同的主线。成功的电影给人的感觉像是“事件”——当然，一旦它们真正起飞，这本身就是一种自我实现的预言，但至少对于大型旗舰大片来说，它们的发行确实带有一种重大事件的真实感觉。
《刺客信条》早已从年度系列的行列中退出 | 图片来源：育碧
这些电影中没有一部是近期电影的续作——最接近的是《蜘蛛侠：崭新之日》，但它距离上一部蜘蛛侠电影已经整整五年了，对于这个现存最具票房号召力的超级英雄IP来说，这是一个相当长的间隔。《奥德赛》的事件地位建立在其导演和明星的个人形象以及其规
articles.original_content:
Modern consumers crave "events", and the games industry needs to provide them | Opinion | GamesIndustry.biz
If you click on a link and make a purchase we may receive a small commission.
Read our editorial policy
.
For almost as long as the games industry has existed, the conventional wisdom around sequels has remained the same: strike while the iron is hot. If you have a hit game, ensure you get a sequel out the door before the public loses interest. If you have more than one hit in a row, that's a franchise, and those need a steady release cadence to ensure the brand's momentum doesn't falter.
No amount of eyerolling about endless sequel-itis or pining for more original games has ever made a dent in that relentless logic. Successful games got rapid sequels; really successful games spawned franchises that publishers would go to great lengths to turn out on as regular a schedule as possible. On some of the biggest franchises, publishers would even swap different development studios in and out across different iterations to ensure that when a new game launched, the next instalment was already deep in development.
My use of the past tense here is deliberate, because over the past decade or so, that approach to sequels and franchises has wavered significantly. Franchises aiming for yearly releases have largely disappeared. Outside of a few remaining sports games that have stuck to the annual release cadence, Call of Duty is essentially the last annual franchise standing. Time between sequels has grown significantly, too. It's now common to see five or six years elapse between a successful game and its follow-up. Not so long ago, there would have been three or four instalments on the market by that stage (or, in many cases, the franchise would already have died on the sharp blade of diminishing returns).
Call of Duty is one of the few remaining annualised franchises, aside from sports games  |
Image credit:
Activision
Some of the reasons for this change are practical. Games take longer to develop than before, and the ability to create post-launch DLC means that full-price sequels need to justify themselves beyond just being new content that doesn't significantly change the core game experience. You could also reasonably argue that some games have gone in the opposite direction – rather than backing away from the rapid release cadence, they have leaned into it, becoming live service titles that launch significant new content multiple times a year.
Even without those factors, however, it's also apparent that audiences' preferences around sequels and franchises have changed significantly. It's not that the voices calling for fewer sequels and more original content have "won". The change is, if anything, more deep-rooted – the fundamental way in which audiences evaluate media and decide where to allocate their money and attention has shifted in a way that's inimical to regular franchise releases.
This shift in consumer behaviour goes well beyond games – in fact, it's arguably easier to see its direct impacts in other media, chiefly movies. This year's major summer releases are a case in point. Cinemagoing itself is clearly still resonating with audiences; in the past few months we've seen massive tentpole releases hurtle towards the billion dollar mark (The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day), indie horror movies earn orders of magnitude more than their budgets off the back of incredible word of mouth (Obsession and Backrooms), and strong showings for sequels to movies from years back (it was seven years since the last Toy Story instalment, and 20 years since the original The Devil Wears Prada).
On the other hand, it's clear that there's not exactly a well-honed formula at work here, because the summer has also seen a lot of major movies failing to get audiences out to multiplexes. Some did fine commercially – Minions & Monsters is only disappointing compared to box office projections and prior releases in the series – but others, like The Mandalorian and Grogu, Moana and Supergirl, have almost certainly lost money, and have cast doubt on entire franchises and cinematic universes.
You can certainly go through each one of those individually and come up with reasons why it did or didn't do well, but there's a through line on all of these, I think. The successful movies felt like
events
– a self-fulfilling prophecy once they really start taking off, of course, but for the big tentpole releases at least, there was a genuine sense of their release being a major event.
Assassin's Creed has long since stepped back from being an annual franchise  |
Image credit:
Ubisoft
None of them is a sequel to an especially recent movie – the closest is Spider-Man: Brand New Day, but it's appearing a solid five years after the last Spider-Man film, which is a pretty long break for the most bankable superhero property in existence. The Odyssey built its event status around the profile of its director and stars, and the scale of its technical ambition. Backrooms and Obsession, meanwhile, whipped up incredible word of mouth and somewhat organically became major event movies in their second and third weeks on release.
By contrast, the poorly performing films lacked all sense of being an event. Moana is a remake of an animated movie from only ten years ago, and Disney has been pumping out these live-action remakes at a rate of at least one a year for the past decade (last year there were two, one of which was the pretty terrible Snow White). The last movie to star the Minions (Despicable Me 4) was only two years ago. Supergirl is coming a year after a Superman movie. And The Mandalorian and Grogu is from a franchise deep in the throes of audience fatigue, as well as being a sequel to several seasons of Disney+ TV shows (it's hard to be an event movie when you're setting homework assignments for your audience).
Game consumers are motivated to engage with something that can genuinely grab attention in a cultural landscap

articles.title: Niko Partners：印度游戏市场突破 10 亿美元，预计 2026 年底达 12 亿美元
articles.summary: Niko Partners报告显示印度游戏市场2025年收入首破10亿美元，玩家达5.11亿，预计2026年底达12亿、2030年达17.7亿美元。移动端收入是主要驱动，非大逃杀手游和UGC平台正获得更多关注。
articles.translated_content:
印度游戏市场突破10亿美元，预计2026年底达12亿美元 | GamesIndustry.biz
如果你点击链接并购买商品，我们可能会获得小额佣金。
请阅读我们的编辑政策。

2025年，印度游戏市场收入首次突破10亿美元，同比增长14.8%，达到10.4亿美元。
根据Niko Partners的数据，预计到2026年收入将达到近12亿美元，到2030年最高可达17.7亿美元——五年复合年增长率为11.2%。

去年玩家总数达到5.11亿。这一数字预计将在2026年超过5.5亿，到2030年达到7亿以上。女性玩家目前占比接近所有玩家的一半，高于2023年的43%。

收入与参与度增长的主要驱动因素是移动游戏支出的增加，这得益于数字化的普及以及“某些消费群体”可支配收入的上升。根据该数据公司的数据，这一细分市场的变现“仍处于早期阶段”，2025年每用户平均收入（ARPU）达到2.04美元，预计到2030年将上升至2.52美元。

Niko Partners还观察到，印度游戏市场正变得更加多元化，玩家开始在PC和主机等平台上探索更广泛的游戏类型。尽管这些受众规模较小，但他们推动了参与度，为发行商提供了在吃鸡和休闲游戏等主流类型之外实现增长的机会。

这一趋势包括用户生成内容的增加，Roblox和Minecraft等平台在印度年轻玩家中越来越受欢迎。此外，非吃鸡类移动游戏占据了更大的市场份额，从2023年6月的53.2%上升至2026年6月的62.8%。

Niko Partners预测，这些领域，加上政府支持的加强、电竞参与度的提升以及发行商机会的扩大，将“塑造印度游戏市场未来五年的发展格局”。

该公司还报告称，印度受众对生成式AI的态度发生了转变。其调查结果显示，玩家“对开发者和玩家如何使用AI变得越来越谨慎。”Niko Partners认为，经济方面的担忧，尤其是AI对就业的影响，是一个关键因素。

articles.original_content:
Niko Partners: India games market exceeds $1bn, forecast to reach $1.2bn by end of 2026 | GamesIndustry.biz
If you click on a link and make a purchase we may receive a small commission.
Read our editorial policy
.
India's games market exceeded $1 billion in revenue for the first time in 2025, up 14.8% year over year to $1.04 billion.
According to
Niko Partners
, revenue is forecast to reach almost $1.2 billion and up to $1.77 billion by 2030 – a five-year CAGR 11.2%.
The total number of players reached 511 million last year. This figure is projected to exceed 550 million in 2026 and reach over 700 million by 2030. Female gamers now represent nearly half of all players, up from 43% in 2023.
The main driver of increased revenue and engagement was higher spending on mobile games, supported by greater digital adoption and rising disposable incomes "among certain consumer segments."
Monetisation for this segment "remains at an early stage," according to the data firm, with average revenue per user (ARPU) reaching $2.04 in 2025 and forecast to rise to $2.52 by 2030.
Niko Partners also observed that India's gaming market is becoming more diverse, with audiences exploring a broader range of genres across platforms such as PC and console.
Although smaller, these audiences drive engagement, providing publishers with the opportunity to grow beyond mainstream genres like battle royale and casual titles.
This trend includes increased user-generated content, with platforms such as Roblox and Minecraft gaining popularity among younger Indian audiences.
Additionally, non-battle royale mobile games captured a larger share of market revenue, rising from 53.2% in June 2023 to 62.8% in June 2026.
Niko Partners predicts that these areas, along with increased government support, rising esports participation, and expanded opportunities for publishers, will "shape India's games market over the next five years."
The firm also reported a shift in Indian audiences' sentiment toward generative AI. Its findings indicate that players "are becoming more cautious about how AI is being used by both developers and players."
Niko Partners identifies economic concerns, especially regarding AI's impact on employment, as a key factor.

articles.translated_content:
根据Game File的独家报道，Netflix将关闭两家游戏工作室，并进一步裁减其内部游戏团队的人员。

这两家工作室分别是位于洛杉矶、开发了《Oxenfree》的Night School，以及赫尔辛基的Moonloot工作室。

据我们了解，Moonloot由前Digital Chocolate、EA和Zynga高管Marko Lastikka领导。

2023年的招聘广告显示，该工作室正在开发一款类似《Animal Crossing》的游戏。

Night School刚刚发布了一款名为《Unhinged》的互动电视类游戏，此前曾与《黑镜》系列创作者Charlie Brooker合作开发一款《Black Mirror》游戏，并推出了《Oxenfree 2》。

Game File还报道称，Netflix内部游戏部门的其他地方也将裁减数量不详的员工。

这家流媒体巨头的发言人对Game File表示：“我们认为在执行上可以更加专注，因此正在对业务进行组织调整，以匹配这些优先事项。”

此前，Netflix独家FIFA世界杯联动游戏的开发工作室已经进行了大规模裁员。

有报道称，该游戏开发商Refactor有多达85%的员工失业。

Netflix还收购并随后关闭了Boss Fight Studios，该工作室最近的项目是免费游玩的、类似《Fall Guys》的派对平台游戏《Squid Game: Unleashed》。

Netflix还在2022年收购了独立解谜工作室Spry Fox，结果该工作室在2025年12月再次独立。

而最引人注目的或许是，它曾成立了一家聚集大牌人才的三A游戏开发工作室，然后又将其关闭。

Netflix在战略和高管层面也经历了不小的变动；2024年，前Epic Games高管Alain Tascan接替了前Netflix游戏业务负责人Mike Verdu，后者于2021年被聘用，负责启动Netflix的游戏业务。

在2025年GDC上，Netflix新任游戏业务负责人Tascan表示，在他的前任Verdu构建起一个满足各种口味的手机游戏目录后，该流媒体平台未来将更加专注于派对游戏、儿童游戏和知名IP。
articles.original_content:
Netflix to close LA studio Night School, Helsinki’s Moonloot and cut internal game teams – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
Netflix is to close two game studios and make further staff cuts to its internal game teams, according to
a Game File scoop
.
The studios in question are LA-based Oxenfree maker Night School and Helsinki studio Moonloot.
We understand Moonloot was
led by former Digital Chocolate, EA and Zynga exec Marko Lastikka.
Job ads from 2023 suggested it was developing an Animal Crossing-like game.
Night School had just shipped an interactive TV-type game called Unhinged, and had previously worked on
a Black Mirror game with series creator Charlie Brooker,
as well as having launched Oxenfree 2.
Game File also reported that an unknown number of staff will be cut from elsewhere in Netflix’s internal games division.
A spokesperson for the streaming giant told Game File: “We see an opportunity to be more focused in our execution, so we are making organizational changes to the business to match those priorities.”
The cuts follow mass layoffs at the development studio behind the Netflix-exclusive FIFA World Cup tie-in game.
Some reports
suggested that up to 85% of staff have lost their jobs at the game’s developer Refactor.
Netflix has also
acquired
then
closed
Boss Fight Studios, whose most recent project was free to play Fall Guys-like party platformer
Squid Game: Unleashed
.
It also
bought indie puzzle studio Spry Fox
back in 2022, only for the studio to
go independent again
back in December 2025.
And perhaps most notoriously it
set up
, then
closed
a triple-A game development studio packed with big-name talent.
Netflix has also seen its fair share of strategy and exec changes; in 2024 former
Epic Games exec Alain Tascan
replaced
former Netflix games boss Mike Verdu
, who was hired to
kickstart Netflix’s gaming efforts
back in 2021.
At GDC 2025, new Netflix games boss Tascan said
that after his predecessor Verdu built out a catalogue of mobile games that catered to all tastes, the streamer would be more focused on party games, kids titles and big-name IP in future.
